children: Average daily ethanol production in the U.S. fell to its lowest level since early May last week, according to data from the Energy Information Administration.

In its latest weekly report published Wednesday, the EIA said that average daily production for the week ended September 18 was 1.028 million barrels a day. That's the lowest rate of production since the week ended May 1, when average production was reported at 1.017 million barrels a day. Total ethanol inventories for the week landed at 24.68 million barrels--a reduction of 537,000 barrels from the prior week.

Both inventories and average production landed on the low side of forecasts from analysts surveyed by Dow Jones, who anticipated production between 1.01 million barrels and 1.134 million barrels a day, along with inventories ranging from 24.52 million barrels to 25.1 million barrels.
Most-active corn futures on the CBOT are trading down 1.4% to $5.43 a bushel Wednesday, ahead of the upcoming summit with U.S. President Trump and Chinese President Xi being held in Washington.
